names: Calcium disodium ethylene diamine tetraacetate, (Calcium disodium EDTA)

more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Calcium disodium EDTA is a calcium-sodium complex of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, used to bind metal ions in food. It binds metal ions, helping control their reactions with other ingredients. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material. EU permissions include canned or bottled fruit and vegetables, heat-treated meat products, unprocessed molluscs and crustaceans, processed fish and fishery products including molluscs and crustaceans.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain sauces; heat–treated meat products; processed fish and fishery products including molluscs and crustaceans; unprocessed molluscs and crustaceans; canned or bottled fruit and vegetables; other fat and oil emulsions including spreads as defined by Council Regulation No 1234/2007 and liquid emulsions.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
